card.statement:
We call ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ quasi-split if $\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}=\emptyset$ and split if in addition $\tau=\text{Id}$ . A split $\imath$ quantum group ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ is the subalgebra of U generated by $B_{i}=F_{i}+\varsigma_{i}E_{i}\tilde{K}^{-1}_{i}+\kappa_{i}\tilde{K}^{-1}_{i}$ $(i\in\mathbb{I})$ ; often $\kappa_{i}=0$ thanks to (1.5). Relations in split ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ are given in (8.1)–(8.2) (with $\mathbb{K}_{i}=-v_{i}^{2}\varsigma_{i}$ ) for ADE type and in (8.9)–(8.10) (with $k=l=0$ ) for BCFG type.

2. (Quasi) K-matrices

As predicted in [8] and established in [2, 36] (also cf. [20]),
there is a unique anti-linear bar involution of the $\mathbb{Q}$ -algebra ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ , denoted by $\psi_{\imath}$ , such that $\psi_{\imath}(v)=v^{-1}$ and

$\displaystyle\psi_{\imath}(B_{i})=B_{i}\;(i\in\mathbb{I}_{\circ}),\quad\psi_{\imath}(F_{j})=F_{j},\quad\psi_{\imath}(E_{j})=E_{j}\;(i\in\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}),\quad\psi_{\imath}(K_{\mu})=K_{-\mu}\;(\mu\in Y^{\imath}).$

The formulation of the quasi $K$ -matrix $\Upsilon$ below (called an intertwiner earlier) was due to Bao and the author [8]; its existence in great generality has been established in [3] (also cf. [9, Remark 4.9]) with additional technicality removed in [10, 36]. The quasi $K$ -matrix for quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type reduces to the quasi $R$ -matrix (cf. [55]).

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
